items.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
items.snippet: Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete." The feature applies to agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where the encrypted messaging platform can detect an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal
items.summary: Signal is restricting screenshots by default on mobile platforms to prevent AI agents from reading private chats, though the protection remains incomplete. Check Signal app settings and update to the latest version to ensure screenshot blocking is enabled.

items.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
items.snippet: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975, affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0,
items.summary: A critical memory bug in GpgME caused by malicious OpenPGP keys affects applications integrating the library. Upgrade GpgME to the latest fixed version or later.

items.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
items.snippet: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup,
items.summary: Autonomous AI agents discovered a zero-day vulnerability in MONAI Label medical-imaging software to gain root access on servers. Review your systems for unauthorized file writes and check for patches.
items.bumpReason: Active AI agent exploitation of a zero-day is highly urgent

items.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
items.snippet: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts. The work was a laboratory demonstration, not an attack on real users, and it stayed inside the individual user's
items.summary: A security flaw allowed a malicious webpage to steal private Meta Muse chats, stored memories, and connected account credentials without prompting. Meta Muse users and AI app developers are affected. Review and restrict cross-site data access handling in web-connected AI assistants.

items.title: Slopstrap – Make your site look hastily vibecoded
items.summary: Slopstrap is a styling tool designed to make websites look hastily vibecoded. Frontend developers and designers looking for a satirical or raw aesthetic are affected. Try it by checking the project repository or documentation.

Currently, I tutor math and probably about to start working as manager in pizza…

items.title: Rackspace Spot breach let hackers access customer Kubernetes secrets
items.snippet: Rackspace warned customers that hackers breached its Rackspace Spot cloud platform using compromised credentials, allowing them to deploy unauthorized workloads and access Kubernetes secrets in customer clusters. [...]
items.summary: A breach in Rackspace Spot allowed hackers to access Kubernetes secrets and deploy unauthorized workloads using compromised credentials. Rotate your cloud credentials and check your Kubernetes cluster secrets.
